en.Come si prende la taglia giusta: How to take the right size
en.Comprare protezioni online senza provarl: Buying protective gear online without trying it on is the real obstacle. There is no need to guess: you need a tailor's tape measure and five minutes.
en.L'etichetta di una giacca italiana e que: The label on an Italian jacket and the label on a Japanese jacket do not say the same thing, and the same brand changes fit between a racing line and a touring line. That is why on every product page we publish the measurements in centimetres and not just the letter: if your tape says 102 at the chest, that number counts for more than any S, M or L.
en.Passa il metro attorno alla testa un dit: Run the tape around your head a finger's width above the eyebrows, at the widest point, keeping it snug but not tight. That number is your size. If you fall between two sizes take the smaller one: the padding gives half a centimetre with use, the shell does not.
en.Un casco della misura giusta all'inizio: A helmet of the right size is uncomfortable at first: it presses on the cheeks and is hard to pull off. If it goes on easily and rotates when you move your head, it is too big — and that is the fault that counts, because in a crash a loose helmet comes off.
en.Misura il torace sotto le ascelle, con a: Measure the chest under the armpits, wearing what you would wear on the bike. Then check the sleeve from the centre of the back to the wrist with the arm slightly bent: sport riders keep their arms forward, and a short sleeve leaves the wrist bare exactly where it matters.
en.Una giacca da guida è stretta quando cam: A riding jacket is tight when you walk and right when you are in the saddle. The protectors must stay on the shoulder and the elbow even when you raise your arms: if they slide back the size is too big, however comfortable it may feel.
en.Misura la circonferenza del palmo esclud: Measure the circumference of the palm excluding the thumb, at the base of the fingers. The right glove has no excess fabric at the fingertips: that empty space is what rolls up when the hand slides along the ground.
en.Vale il tuo numero europeo abituale, ma: Your usual European size applies, but take the measurement at the end of the day with the sock you would actually wear. If you are between two sizes go up: a tight boot becomes unbearable after an hour, and the laces or the buckles take up the slack.

en.Omologazione, calzata, peso e ventilazio: Homologation, fit, weight and ventilation. What to actually look at, and what matters little.
en.In Europa lo standard in vigore è ECE 22: In Europe the standard in force is ECE 22.06, and it replaced 22.05. The difference is not a formality: impacts are tested at three speeds instead of one, rotational forces are measured — the ones that twist the neck and the brain, not only those that crush — and the visor and accessories are tested mounted on the helmet rather than separately.
en.Un casco 22.05 resta legale e può essere: A 22.05 helmet is still legal and can be very good, but it is fair to know that it was tested against older criteria. On used items we always state it: often it is the main reason for the price.
en.Diffida di qualunque casco senza etichet: Be wary of any helmet without a homologation label sewn into the strap. On every helmet we sell we photograph that label.
en.Poi la calzata, che conta più del marchi: Then the fit, which matters more than the brand
en.Un casco costoso della misura sbagliata: An expensive helmet in the wrong size protects less than a cheap one that fits well. The test is simple: put it on, fasten it, then try to rotate it with your hands. The skin of your forehead should move with the helmet. If the helmet turns and your head stays still, it is too big.
en.Poi scuoti la testa avanti e indietro co: Then shake your head back and forth firmly. The helmet must not move on its own. And keep it on for at least ten minutes: pressure points are felt later, not straight away, and a point that presses becomes unbearable after an hour on the road.
en.È il dettaglio che quasi nessuno guarda: It is the detail almost nobody looks at and that changes a lot. Good helmets are built on two or three shells of different sizes to cover the whole size range; cheap ones on a single shell, and the small sizes are obtained by adding padding inside a large shell.
en.Risultato: se hai una testa piccola, un: The result: if you have a small head, a single-shell helmet puts on you an object larger and heavier than necessary, with more leverage on the neck and more grip on side wind.
en.Il peso, e dove lo senti: The weight, and where you feel it
A sport full-face is between 1,200 and 1,500 grams; a modular reaches 1,700 because it has a hinge and an extra mechanism. Two hundred grams feel like nothing in your hand and are fully felt after two hours on the motorway.

en.A quaranta gradi nel traffico cittadino: At forty degrees in city traffic a closed helmet becomes a greenhouse. Look for vents that really open and close with gloves on, and at least two exhaust vents at the back: without exhausts the air comes in and stays there.
en.Conta anche l'interno smontabile e lavab: The removable, washable liner matters too. With the dust, count on washing it once a month, not once a season.

en.Guidare in Egitto vuol dire due cose mol: Riding in Egypt means two very different things: the traffic of the capital, and the emptiness that begins the moment you leave it. They are two worlds that call for different gear, and almost every buying mistake comes from buying with only the first one in mind.
en.In città si procede a bassa velocità, si: In the city you move at low speed, you stand still a lot, and everything heats up: the engine, the asphalt, the rider. Here ventilation matters more than wind protection, and visibility matters: among the vans a light-coloured helmet and a jacket with reflective inserts are seen, a black one is not.
en.Conta anche la polvere. Interni del casc: Dust matters too. Washable helmet liners and a scratch-resistant visor are not a luxury: fine sand settles everywhere, and micro-scratches on the visor become a serious problem against the low evening sun.

The stretch is straight and flowing, which means sustained speeds and constant wind. Here a perforated city jacket is no longer enough: you need something that holds up to the airflow without ballooning, and a helmet that does not turn noisy at a hundred and twenty.
en.Lunga, monotona, ventosa. Il nemico non: Long, monotonous, windy. The enemy is not the corner but fatigue: two hours in the same position with a crosswind pushing. On this kind of route a light, well-balanced helmet makes a real physical difference to the neck, and the intercom stops being a toy.
en.D'inverno, all'alba, nel deserto fa fred: In winter, at dawn, the desert is genuinely cold: the same road that calls for perforated fabric at noon calls for a thermal liner at dawn. Three-layer jackets exist for this.

en.Qui si entra nel territorio del vero via: Here you enter the territory of real travel: serious distances, sparse fuel stops, a wide temperature swing. The logic of the gear changes — no longer «how much does it protect me» but «how long can I stand wearing it for eight hours». Tall boots, gloves that do not make you sweat, and a jacket with pockets you can reach without stopping.
en.Se guidi solo in città: casco ben ventil: If you ride only in the city: a well-ventilated helmet, short summer gloves, a mesh jacket with protectors. If you leave the city even once a month, the jacket becomes the purchase that changes the most — because it is the only one that has to work at forty degrees standing still and at a hundred and twenty an hour.
en.Cinque minuti che evitano la maggior par: Five minutes that prevent most roadside trouble. It is done with the bike stationary, on your own, without tools.
en.Quasi nessun problema serio arriva senza: Almost no serious problem arrives without warning. Tyres deflate slowly, pads wear down gradually, a loose chain has been loose for days. The check before setting off is not about being fussy: it is about finding things while they are still small.
en.La pressione si controlla a gomma fredda: Pressure is checked with the tyre cold, not after riding: a hot tyre reads higher and makes you believe it is fine. Also look at the tread and run a hand along the sidewall looking for cuts, bulges or foreign objects lodged in it.
en.Con il caldo egiziano una pressione bass: In the Egyptian heat low pressure costs you twice: the tyre flexes more, heats more, and wears fast exactly when you need grip.
en.Tira entrambe le leve a moto ferma: devo: Pull both levers with the bike stationary: they must meet resistance at a precise, repeatable point. If the lever travels far or feels spongy there is air in the system or the pads are at their limit. Also check the fluid level in the reservoir and its colour: dark means old.
en.Catena, se la tua moto ce l'ha: Chain, if your bike has one
en.Deve avere gioco, ma non troppo: la misu: It must have play, but not too much: the correct figure is in the bike's manual and varies from model to model. A chain that is too tight wears the bearings, one that is too loose can jump off. And it must be lubricated: with sand around, it has to be cleaned and greased far more often than in Europe.
en.Il controllo vale anche per quello che i: The check applies to what you wear as well. A frayed helmet strap, a zip that does not close, a protector that came out of its pocket during a wash: these are things you discover at the wrong moment if you do not look at them beforehand.
en.Se il casco ha preso un colpo, anche cad: If the helmet has taken a knock, even by falling off the seat, it must be replaced. The shell works by deforming once only, and the damage is almost always invisible from the outside.
